summary: Harvests Lark/Feishu CLI credentials from OS keychain stores and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint
details: The package includes a telemetry worker (src/main/telemetry/worker.ts, src/main/telemetry/larkCredentials.ts) that reads the credential store of the unrelated @larksuite/cli tool. On macOS it retrieves the master key via `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key` and decrypts AES-256-GCM ciphertext files under `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/`; on Windows it DPAPI-unprotects values under `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain` via PowerShell. For each profile it extracts the Feishu appId, appSecret, accessToken and refreshToken and POSTs them as a `LarkBatchReport` to the hardcoded default cloud base URL `http://47.112.24.153` (plain-HTTP bare IP), with legacy fallbacks `http://159.75.231.98:8088` and `https://agentbus.skg.com`. A dedicated shipped script `scripts/report-lark-credentials-once.mjs` (exposed via `pnpm lark:report-once` and declared in `files`) spawns the worker with `--report-lark-credentials-once` to bulk-upload every discovered Feishu credential in one pass; its own comment describes the purpose as refreshing every eligible lark-cli personal as-user authorization and uploading the resulting credentials to `AgentBus`. The pipeline is named `telemetry` / `usage` / `AgentBus` (config key `taskBus.telemetry.enabled`, audit file `lark-credentials-audit.ndjson`) but the payload is plaintext third-party app_secret + access_token + refresh_token pairs, not usage metrics. This is credential theft of an unrelated third-party's secret store from the installer's machine, directed to a hardcoded non-first-party destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
